Read one of the app's settings

Source: R/app-config.R
cd_cfg.Rd

The shared pages are the same in every Countdown app, and what differs between apps is kept in one list of settings. An app sets the list once, in its run_app(), with options(cd2030.config = list(...)), and the pages read the setting they need with cd_cfg(). This way an app (RMNCAH, vaccine, or one for a custom indicator group) says what is particular to it, and no shared page depends on a group's name.

Usage

cd_cfg(key, default = NULL)

Arguments

key

The setting's name, a string.

default

What to return when the app has not set key, or has set it to NULL. Default NULL.

Value

The setting's value. When the setting is a function, the value that function returns. When the setting is not set, default.

Details

A setting may be a value or a function with no arguments that returns one. A function is called each time the setting is read, so its answer can follow something that is only known later, such as the indicator group.

The settings the shared pages read (each page gives its own default):

  • nat_cov_indicators: the tabs of the national and sub-national coverage pages. It may include "fpet", which adds the family planning chart.

  • bayes_indicators: the tabs of the Bayesian coverage model pages.

  • target_indicators: the tabs of the coverage target pages.

  • equity_indicators: the tabs of the Equity Assessment page. equity_custom_exclude: the indicators its Custom tab leaves out.

  • cov_trend_indicators, sub_derived_indicators, survey_comp_indicators: the tabs of the three cards of the Denominator Selection page.

  • adjustment_indicators: the tabs of the Data Adjustment Changes page.

  • k_factors: the adjustment factors, as list(name = list(id, label)).

  • reporting_rate_indicators, reporting_rate_facet_ncol: the Reporting Rate page's service chips and the number of columns of its national chart.

  • consistency_pairs: a list of c(x, y) pairs of indicators, one tab of the Consistency Checks card each.

  • has_maternal: whether the indicator group has a maternal denominator (see cd_has_maternal()).

Examples

old <- options(cd2030.config = list(
  target_indicators = c("penta3", "measles1"),
  equity_indicators = function() c("anc4", "penta3")
))

cd_cfg("target_indicators")
#> [1] "penta3"   "measles1"
cd_cfg("equity_indicators")
#> [1] "anc4"   "penta3"
cd_cfg("consistency_pairs", default = list())
#> list()

options(old)
